sense: a piece of a tree trunk

terms.gloss: a log, a stake, a tree trunk
evidence: Ov. Fast. 5.506: ignis in hesternō stīpite parvus erat
terms.comment: A log or a post, cut or lying; also, like English “blockhead”, an insult for a dull person (Ter. Heaut. 5.1.4: caudex, stīpes, asinus).

evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.1.69: ligna et sarmenta circumdare (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In this sense classically only plural; lignum is wood as a material (see wood), and timber for building is māteria.
The trunk of a tree, standing or felled; also the trunk of the body.

phrases.latin: dissolve frīgus ligna super focō largē repōnēns
phrases.english: melt the cold away, piling logs on the hearth without stint

phrases.latin: ignis in hesternō stīpite parvus erat
phrases.english: there was a small fire in yesterday’s log

phrases.latin: Quaerendus cuneus est malus truncō malō.
phrases.english: a hard log needs a hard wedge

sources: Lewis & Short: stipes · Lewis & Short: lignum · Lewis & Short: truncus
